Children as young as infants were separated from parents, with many held in wire-mesh enclosures that Democrats and advocates called 'cages.' Some children were separated for months or years, with parents deported without their children, creating international human rights violations. Trump initially denied responsibility, falsely claiming the separations were required by law and blaming Democrats. When public outcry became overwhelming, Trump ended the policy while falsely taking credit for solving a problem his own administration created. The family separation policy represented one of the most severe human rights violations in modern American history, with UN experts calling it 'unconscionable' and a violation of children's rights. Many families have never been reunited, and the trauma inflicted on thousands of children represents a permanent stain on American history.

frozen_record.description_long: After Attorney General William Barr resigned in December 2020, Donald Trump pressed acting Attorney General Jeffrey Rosen to have the Justice Department support the campaign’s election lawsuits and investigate claims of voter fraud. Rosen refused, citing the department’s findings that there was no significant fraud. Trump then sought to replace Rosen with Jeffrey Clark, a Justice Department official who had told Trump he believed fraud affected the result. When Rosen learned of the plan, he and Deputy Attorney General Richard Donoghue contacted other senior officials; they agreed they would resign if Clark took over. On January 3, Rosen and Donoghue met with Trump, Clark and White House lawyers. Rosen, Donoghue and White House Counsel Pat Cipollone urged Trump not to proceed, while Justice Department legal chief Steven Engel said he would resign and others would follow. After nearly three hours, Trump decided not to fire Rosen. The episode shows an effort to use departmental leadership to advance election claims and the officials’ response. The title’s “steal the election” wording is a characterization, not a quoted legal finding.
